steps.name: Juana
steps.text: Thank you for dinner, Javi. It was delicious.

steps.name: Javier
steps.text: Señora Juana... I have some questions.

steps.name: Juana
steps.text: Go on then, no need to hold back.

steps.name: Javier
steps.text: I feel it's a little... risky, to be hunting such a massive saltfin with the men we have.

steps.name: Javier
steps.text: Wouldn't it be safer to go after a school of smaller ones?

steps.name: Juana
steps.text: The saltfin schools we've reeled in have been far too small. We'll need a lot more alchemical materials for what is to come.

steps.name: Javier
steps.text: We've already prepared plenty.

steps.name: Juana
steps.text: Still far from enough. The compass was just the beginning. We'll need so much more once we enter the ocean.

steps.name: Javier
steps.text: Poz, the last cook, said you like to make some crazy decisions. Most of the time, it makes our blood run hot with excitement.

steps.name: Javier
steps.text: But other times, it makes our blood turn to ice.

steps.name: Juana
steps.text: ...Yet he was ever-loyal to me, supporting even those decisions that made him freeze up inside.

steps.name: Javier
steps.text: Is that what you expect from me too?

steps.name: Juana
steps.text: No. Which is why he's the previous cook and you're the new one.

steps.name: Juana
steps.text: Do you really wish to spend the rest of your life worrying about your next meal? This is our chance. Seize it, and all our problems vanish forever.

steps.name: Juana
steps.text: The ocean managed to nurture the entirety of the Golden Age, but our entire fleet can't even compare to your average gang of smugglers.

steps.name: Javier
steps.text: But the Salt Flat has nurtured us for decades! It hasn't been easy, but you've led us through the years.

steps.name: Juana
steps.text: The Flat is too barren for us.

steps.name: Javier
steps.text: And the ocean is too dangerous for us.

steps.name: Juana
steps.text: Think about the townsfolk. They would like nothing more than to be rid of us, and their net draws ever closer.

steps.name: Javier
steps.text: You were never afraid of them!

steps.name: Juana
steps.text: It's not them that I'm afraid of.

steps.name: Juana
steps.text: It's the Flat. Its ecosystem is about to collapse.

steps.name: Juana
steps.text: That fissure was just the beginning. Survey teams are reporting that large voids have appeared beneath the Salt Flat, where underground rivers have dried up.

steps.name: Javier
steps.text: Voids?

steps.name: Juana
steps.text: The underground rivers are drying up. The number of microorganisms has dropped sharply, and with it, the number of saltfins that feed upon them.

steps.name: Juana
steps.text: It's been a long time since one of our finships encountered a large school of saltfins.

steps.name: Javier
steps.text: Why didn't you tell us?

steps.name: Juana
steps.text: What was I supposed to say? That we're finished if we don't escape this place? What would that accomplish other than causing a panic?

steps.name: Javier
steps.text: Is this the only way then?

steps.name: Juana
steps.text: ...Yes, it's the only way.

steps.name: Isidro
steps.text: A little to the left... thanks.

steps.name: Nene
steps.text: Mmph!

steps.name: Isidro
steps.text: Yes... now a little harder.

steps.name: Nene
steps.text: Mmph—!

steps.name: Isidro
steps.text: That was a long day, learning to catch saltfins with Señor Rus... Ow, my aching shoulders...

steps.name: Isidro
steps.text: Mm, yes, that's the spot.
Nene stomps even harder on Isidro's back as he inhales and exhales deeply.

steps.name: Isidro
steps.text: Nene...

steps.name: Nene
steps.text: Mm-ph!

steps.name: Isidro
steps.text: Never mind, you wouldn't understand.

steps.name: Isidro
steps.text: ...It's not like I don't want to help you all.

steps.name: Isidro
steps.text: When I was little, a beggar taught me a few tricks, just to earn scraps on the streets.

steps.name: Isidro
steps.text: But when I met my mentor, he told me those weren't tricks.

steps.name: Isidro
steps.text: It was alchemy.

steps.name: Nene
steps.text: Mm... hmph...

steps.name: Isidro
steps.text: I was fascinated by alchemical studies. It earned me praise from my mentor, and recognition from my peers.

steps.name: Isidro
steps.text: And most importantly, I was no longer a street urchin with nothing to my name.

steps.name: Isidro
steps.text: I was worth something.

steps.name: Isidro
steps.text: That is, until I learned the most fundamental nature of that school of alchemy...
Isidro pauses. Nene stops stomping and looks up perplexedly.

a.text: You can never abandon what you have, Isidro.
You fear you will go back to having nothing if you fail.
But the nature of alchemy is to achieve your goal, devoting everything to it, no matter the cost.
The stakes, everything... The return, a chance.
Why is it that only our alchemy was used to sail the seas? Because the ocean demands such quality.

steps.text: Sensing Isidro's depression, Nene lies down on his back and chirps gently.

steps.name: Isidro
steps.text: Rus was right. You all just want to live a decent life. Repairing the compass and going to sea... It's not worth the risk.

steps.name: Isidro
steps.text: But I'm curious... how exactly is Juana's compass constructed?

steps.name: Isidro
steps.text: The Corazonix inside... does it truly point towards whatever your heart yearns for the most, as the stories say?

steps.name: Isidro
steps.text: If I just had the chance to study it...

steps.name: Isidro
steps.text: Did you fall asleep?

steps.name: Isidro
steps.text: I'm curious. What's going on in my own heart?

steps.name: Anastasio
steps.text: Flowers?

steps.name: Silver
steps.text: Doctor Añora was the first to plant them in town, decades ago. For use in ointments.

steps.name: Anastasio
steps.text: Ah... I have seen them before, in the halls of the Bastión de Cánticos.

steps.name: Silver
steps.text: I've never been.

steps.name: Silver
steps.text: All I know is that it is the first flower to bloom from the salted earth of Aarón, after so many years of being besieged by the sea.

steps.name: Silver
steps.text: The townsfolk used to give me these, as a token of appreciation I think.

steps.name: Silver
steps.text: Now, I feel I should be offering them to you.

steps.name: Anastasio
steps.text: No, señor, I am unworthy.

steps.name: Silver
steps.text: Had you not taken those... measures towards the caravans, to obtain the predator burdenbeasts...

steps.name: Silver
steps.text: We could never have gone after those despicable bandits in the Salt Flat.

steps.name: Anastasio
steps.text: I did no more than what must be done.

steps.name: Silver
steps.text: Your duty, of course.

steps.name: Silver
steps.text: I believe you mentioned you are after a forbidden relic the bandits have stolen.

steps.name: Silver
steps.text: What sort of relic could it possibly be, to bring you all the way to this barren land?

steps.name: Anastasio
steps.text: A... compass.

steps.name: Silver
steps.text: There are thousands of antique compasses from old Iberia.

steps.name: Anastasio
steps.text: None like this. This one corrupts the heart.

steps.name: Anastasio
steps.text: It points towards the user's deepest desires, dredged from the depths of the heart... Or so it is said.

steps.name: Anastasio
steps.text: But those who cast their eyes towards such base desires can never turn back.

steps.name: Anastasio
steps.text: It drives them to theft, robbery, murder. They cannot stop themselves, try as they might.

steps.name: Silver
steps.text: ...You really think so?

steps.name: Anastasio
steps.text: It is simply the truth.

steps.name: Silver
steps.text: Is this what you've been preaching to the townsfolk these past few days?

steps.name: Anastasio
steps.text: It was not I who preached. The people here already understood this truth, more profoundly than I ever have.

steps.name: Anastasio
steps.text: Someone had already revealed it to them. Perhaps you?

steps.name: Silver
steps.text: ...Yes, it was me.

steps.name: Silver
steps.text: It was I who issued those prohibitions.

steps.name: Anastasio
steps.text: Why stop then? Why lift the prohibition?

steps.name: Silver
steps.text: Look at this town. No one here dares touch the new goods and technologies that the caravans bring. No one dares leave their house after dark.

steps.name: Silver
steps.text: They dare not fill their stomachs... even in years of plenty.

steps.name: Silver
steps.text: Every word I used to shackle these poor people has continued to shackle them.

steps.name: Anastasio
steps.text: They see it differently.

steps.name: Anastasio
steps.text: Was it not your deeds that helped them lay aside their dreams and laments for wealth and power. Was it not your words that encouraged them to take up the hoe and the scythe?

steps.name: Silver
steps.text: Times have changed, Señor Alguacil.

steps.name: Anastasio
steps.text: Times never change, Señor Calificador.

steps.name: Anastasio
steps.text: The deepest desires of the heart should never be probed. Not by anyone, not anywhere.

steps.name: Anastasio
steps.text: Never.

steps.name: Excited Sailor
steps.text: Saltfins ahoy!

steps.name: Excited Sailor
steps.text: Two meters wide, eighteen long!

steps.name: Teach
steps.text: Now that's a big one. Chase 'em down!

steps.name: Juana
steps.text: Full speed ahead! Harpoons ready!

steps.name: Teach
steps.text: Hard to port! Full speed!
Harpoons up! Hey, ho!♪
In the waves the big one rolls!♪
Stomp the planks! Hoist the sails!♪
Drown the high wind's wail!♪
Hey, ho! Up we go!♪
Before the sun sinks low!♪

steps.name: Rus
steps.text: Wha'cha watching from a corner for, chaval?

steps.name: Isidro
steps.text: Oh, nothing...

steps.name: Isidro
steps.text: Ugh!

steps.name: Rus
steps.text: Watch yourself. But the shaking is a good thing. Means we're getting close.

steps.name: Rus
steps.text: Where'd the boss put you? Reeling in the net from here, or joining the hunt in the salts?

steps.name: Isidro
steps.text: Señora Juana won't let me leave the ship.

steps.name: Rus
steps.text: I don't get it. With your swordhand, you'd be way more useful in the hunt.

steps.name: Isidro
steps.text: She didn't give me any particular job either. Just told me to do whatever I can.

steps.name: Rus
steps.text: Weird. She's usually so detailed.

steps.name: Isidro
steps.text: Maybe the standards are laxer for the new guy?

steps.name: Excited Sailor
steps.text: I see it!

steps.name: Composed Sailor
steps.text: Finshit... that's a BIG one...

steps.name: Excited Sailor
steps.text: Lower the boat! Don't let it get away!

steps.name: Composed Sailor
steps.text: Wait, it's turning!

steps.name: Teach
steps.text: Full rudder! It's running into us!

steps.name: Juana
steps.text: Not in the best mood, big guy? Well, my mood couldn't be better.

spans.text: Not in the best mood, big guy? Well,

steps.name: Juana
steps.text: Change of plans, Perlita. Javier stays aboard. I'll lead the hunt myself.

steps.name: Teach
steps.text: But señora, you haven't led a hunt in ages.

steps.name: Juana
steps.text: Do as I say!

steps.name: Teach
steps.text: Javier! Come back! Take the helm!

steps.name: Javier
steps.text: It's too dangerous, señora!

steps.name: Juana
steps.text: This one's too much for you, Javi. Stay on the ship. I need you to work with me.

steps.name: Javier
steps.text: Then what should I do?

steps.name: Juana
steps.text: See that salt reef in the shape of a tongue? Herd it there with salt rounds. I'll handle the rest.

steps.name: Javier
steps.text: Aye aye.

steps.name: Teach
steps.text: Full rudder! Hang tight!
The salt ship makes a hard turn to starboard, but not quite quickly enough to avoid brushing against the side of the charging saltfin.
Cold sweat rolls down everyone's backs at the grating sound. Hanging onto a fence for dear life, Isidro looks towards where the sound came from.
He sees a massive saltfin swim past the ship, sending stinging salt grains flying across the deck.

steps.name: Isidro
steps.text: How could a saltfin grow this big?

steps.name: Isidro
steps.text: I thought that last one was the biggest I'd ever see...

steps.name: Rus
steps.text: No, chaval... Even I've never seen one this big.

steps.name: Isidro
steps.text: What?

steps.name: Rus
steps.text: We never hunt ones this big, not by choice.

steps.name: Rus
steps.text: This is loco! We're in way over our heads!

steps.name: Teach
steps.text: Load! Aim! Fire!

steps.name: Teach
steps.text: Port broadside! Fire!

steps.name: Javier
steps.text: Aim for the eyes and nostril! Hitting the shell won't do a damn thing!

steps.name: Javier
steps.text: Is Señora Juana in position?

steps.name: Rus
steps.text: Boss! Boss!

steps.name: Teach
steps.text: She just went down!

steps.name: Rus
steps.text: You gotta stop the hunt! We're in way over our heads!

steps.name: Teach
steps.text: And how would we eat tomorrow if we don't hunt today?

steps.name: Javier
steps.text: What's the matter, Rus?

steps.name: Rus
steps.text: It's twice as big as any other saltfin. Only the leader of a school could grow this big.

steps.name: Rus
steps.text: So you'd expect it to have a whole school behind it, but I sure don't see one.

steps.name: Teach
steps.text: Get to the point, professor.

steps.name: Rus
steps.text: Either it lost its school, or it was abandoned. Either way, it's mad. Real mad.

steps.name: Javier
steps.text: Does Señora Juana know about this?

steps.name: Teach
steps.text: It was her plan.

steps.name: Rus
steps.text: She's toying with our lives again. If that thing decides to bring us down with it, we're all—

steps.name: Rus
steps.text: Mm...

steps.name: Javier
steps.text: Teach...

steps.name: Teach
steps.text: Señora and the hunting team have already left. It's too late to back down.

steps.name: Teach
steps.text: Don't let the rest of the crew know. We can't afford a panic.

steps.name: Teach
steps.text: Keep firing, Javier.

steps.name: Teach
steps.text: I'd rather die on a hunt today than of starvation in a month.

steps.name: Nervous Sailor
steps.text: Boss... Can we really take on this big guy?

steps.name: Juana
steps.text: Of course. And we'll win.

steps.name: Juana
steps.text: Wait for it to turn and aim for gaps in its shell! If you can hit the nostril, all the better!

steps.name: Nervous Sailor
steps.text: It's coming straight for us!

steps.name: Juana
steps.text: Row! Hard forward!

steps.name: Excited Sailor
steps.text: Aye aye!

steps.name: Juana
steps.text: Harpoons ready! ...Now!

steps.name: Excited Sailor
steps.text: Argh!

steps.name: Juana
steps.text: Good! Keep it up!

steps.name: Nervous Sailor
steps.text: It's too strong! I can't hold this rope much longer!

steps.name: Excited Sailor
steps.text: I'm with you!

steps.name: Juana
steps.text: All hands! Again!

steps.name: Sailors
steps.text: Argh!

steps.name: Juana
steps.text: Good! Someone hit the nostril!

steps.name: Juana
steps.text: Hold that rope like your life depends on it!

steps.name: Sailors
steps.text: Hah!

steps.name: Excited Sailor
steps.text: Thirty meters left!

steps.name: Juana
steps.text: Keep holding on!

steps.name: Excited Sailor
steps.text: Twenty meters!

steps.name: Excited Sailor
steps.text: Ten meters!

steps.name: Nervous Sailor
steps.text: We're out of rope!

steps.name: Juana
steps.text: Just a little more!

steps.name: Excited Sailor
steps.text: It's coming out of the salt layer!

steps.name: Juana
steps.text: Now! Reel it in!
Juana rides her boat towards the saltfin as the rope is reeled in. Its thick hide has been pierced by dozens of harpoons, blood seeping out from the wounds.
Listening to its heavy, rapid breathing, Juana knows that its life is coming to an end.

She cannot help but place her hand on the massive figure, feeling its life flow out of it little by little, until the saltfin closes its eyes, still raging against the dying of the light with its last breath.

steps.name: Nervous Sailor
steps.text: Phew... finally.

steps.name: Excited Sailor
steps.text: We did it!

steps.name: Juana
steps.text: ...Hail the salt ship. Have them come for us.

steps.name: Excited Sailor
steps.text: Aye aye!

steps.name: Juana
steps.text: Wait!

steps.name: Nervous Sailor
steps.text: Look out, señora!

steps.name: Excited Sailor
steps.text: It's not dead yet...
Juana feels a gaze filled with overwhelming malice upon her.
She looks up at its eyes, filled with hatred and anger.
The next instant, the saltfin begins flailing violently, sending blood-stained salt flying, falling over the sailors like rain.
It breaks free of the ropes, leaving behind only the harpoons still impaled in its hide.
It raises its tail fin high.

steps.name: Nervous Sailor
steps.text: Retreat! Retreat!

steps.name: Excited Sailor
steps.text: No...
Several boats are quickly snapped in two by the saltfin's attack, and the air is filled with the screams of injured sailors.
The sound seems to fill Juana with a certain resolve. She charges towards the rampaging saltfin, and grabs one of the harpoons on its back.
It leaps up, trying to shake her off.

steps.name: Excited Sailor
steps.text: It's too dangerous, señora! Let go!

steps.name: Juana
steps.text: No! This one is mine, as long as I still breathe!
The saltfin sweeps aside the boats in front of it and swims into the distance, carrying Juana on its back.
It does so with astounding speed, like an arrow from a bow, or a dying star.

steps.name: Javier
steps.text: Faster!

steps.name: Javier
steps.text: We have to catch it!

steps.name: Teach
steps.text: Stop! Stop! That's as far as we can go! The beast dragged Juana into the Skeletal Reef!

steps.name: Rus
steps.text: Javier... Javier...

steps.name: Teach
steps.text: You were right, Rus. I shouldn't have knocked you out.

steps.name: Rus
steps.text: Not the first time. I know how you can get.

steps.name: Rus
steps.text: But listen for once... We can't chase her. The steam in Skeletal Reef will tear our ship apart.

steps.name: Javier
steps.text: If you won't go, give me a boat. I'll find her.

steps.name: Rus
steps.text: No one survives that place! Not us, not...

steps.name: Javier
steps.text: Juana can.

steps.name: Javier
steps.text: Are you with me or not, Teach?

steps.name: Teach
steps.text: Don't be reckless, Javier!

steps.name: Javier
steps.text: You're just gonna let her die?

steps.name: Teach
steps.text: No one wants to lose our leader. But we can't lose you too.

steps.name: Teach
steps.text: She liked you. If something happens to her, you have a responsibility for what comes next.

steps.name: Teach
steps.text: I'll go.

steps.name: Javier
steps.text: Maybe so, Teach. But she won't die. I won't let her!

steps.name: Javier
steps.text: Who's with me?!

steps.name: Bold Sailor
steps.text: Count me in!

steps.name: Loyal Sailor
steps.text: And me!
Would you mind if I join you?
The sailors part to let Isidro through.

steps.name: Javier
steps.text: If it isn't our resident alchemist. I figured you'd keep your mouth shut forever.

steps.name: Javier
steps.text: What could you possibly do, chaval?

steps.name: Isidro
steps.text: I can help you get out of that valley alive.

steps.name: Warrior Priest
steps.text: We're ready, Señor Silver.

steps.name: Silver
steps.text: Good. Take them in at my command.

steps.name: Warrior Priest
steps.text: Yes, sir!

steps.name: Silver
steps.text: ...Are you sure those bandits will pass through here, Señor Alguacil?

steps.name: Anastasio
steps.text: Yes... they're short on supplies.

steps.name: Anastasio
steps.text: Saltfins are their only food source in the Salt Flat. From what the caravans tell us, they must travel through this passage when they return from a hunt.

steps.name: Anastasio
steps.text: Exhausted by their quarry, they will be no match for us.

steps.name: Silver
steps.text: Good.

steps.name: Silver
steps.text: With this ambush, it will all be over.

steps.name: Silver
steps.text: Things will improve in town once we have the bandits' technology and supplies.

steps.name: Silver
steps.text: Right, Anastasio?
Anastasio mutters something, but Silver does not hear it.
He simply gazes upon the vast Salt Flat before him, as if seeing the town's prosperous future out there.
